beats.narration: Where does that state come from? A small input module reads the sensor. On the wireless mesh it shows up as a Modbus device. Modbus is an industrial wiring and data standard many sensors speak.
beats.caption: Input module reads the sensor, a Modbus device on the mesh
evidence: integration-and-devices#L01 (live_today yes: a lightning node is a Modbus asset on the mesh, reached through an input module; a radio node on site reads the lightning warning unit and reports its state across the mesh); lead decision C: the sensor is read through a small input module and shows up on the mesh as a Modbus device

Modbus is explained once, here at first mention, in the approved wording: an industrial wiring and data standard many sensors speak; the lane badge reads WIRELESS MESH + MODBUS INPUT; no brand named for the module

beats.narration: A gateway passes the readings to the cloud, then to this page, and anything unreadable is set aside.
beats.caption: Anything unreadable is set aside
evidence: integration-and-devices#L02 (live_today yes: lightning messages go to their own queue; messages that cannot be parsed go to a separate queue. Caveat: queue and rule existence were not verified live, so narration and caption say only set aside, never never lost)

integration-and-devices#W10 and #L08 (messages with no registered handler or an unassigned device are not stored as status) are why the narration says the gateway passes the readings on, not that every message arrives; the WAKECAP PORTAL sink box that appears at this stage is the page narrated as 'this page'; Modbus was explained in l10, not repeated
